<!-- name: Detection Intelligence -->
<!-- board: See why each detection matched | Tune alerts by detection type | Trust, ignore, or always alert | Browse chronological EVENTS history -->

**Detection Intelligence.** v1.21.0 makes SquachWatch much more explicit about
*why* something was detected, *how often* it has been seen, *whether it is
moving closer or farther away*, and *what the device should do about that
specific target*. The release adds per-type alert rules, persistent per-device
policies, chronological event history, and richer RSSI context while preserving
the existing fixed-size data paths and the v1.20.1 release pipeline.

**Added**
- **Concrete detection evidence.** Live detections now record the actual match
  source: BLE manufacturer ID, service UUID, advertised name, Find My payload,
  iBeacon payload, Wi-Fi OUI, SSID, Pwnagotchi, evil-twin, or deauthentication
  evidence. ALERT, LOG and MORE INFO expose that source instead of forcing the
  user to infer why a classification happened.
- **~15-second RSSI history and trend.** Each live detection keeps eight
  allocation-free RSSI samples and reports LEARNING, APPROACHING, STEADY, or
  MOVING AWAY. ALERT gets a live sparkline; LOG shows direction plus a compact
  row sparkline where the layout has room.
- **Uniform sighting counts.** A dedicated saturating repeat counter gives alert
  rules a consistent meaning across BLE, Wi-Fi and deauth. Deauth keeps raw
  frame count in `hits` while `repeats` counts qualifying bursts, so one noisy
  burst cannot masquerade as multiple independent sightings.
- **Per-type Alert Rules.** Every detection type can independently choose full
  alert or LOG ONLY, inherit or override the global confidence threshold,
  require 1/2/3/5 sightings, use OFF/30s/1m/5m/15m cooldown, and decide whether
  a normal signature alert may wake a sleeping display. Defaults preserve the
  previous v1.20.1 behavior.
- **Device Policies.** Persistent NORMAL / IGNORE / TRUSTED / ALWAYS ALERT
  behavior replaces the old IGNORE-only model. IGNORE and TRUSTED continue to
  count and log detections while suppressing interruption. ALWAYS ALERT can
  bypass per-type log-only/confidence/repeat/cooldown rules plus device snooze
  and AUTO SNOOZE, but it does not override DETECTION FILTER or lock-screen
  alert security.
- **Chronological EVENTS history.** LOG now switches between the existing
  one-row-per-device DEVICES view and an EVENTS view showing every persisted
  FIRST/BACK sighting newest-first. Event rows include time, type, MAC, RSSI,
  confidence, hit count, identity, current HERE/GONE state, and current
  non-normal policy when applicable.
- **Read-only historical EVENTS.** WATCH/HUNT/policy long-press actions remain
  DEVICES-only, preventing an old historical row from being mistaken for a
  currently actionable live device.

**Changed**
- WATCH keeps its existing special behavior and remains separate from ALWAYS
  ALERT. It still bypasses AUTO SNOOZE through the dedicated WATCH alert path,
  but does not become a blanket bypass for confidence, repeat, cooldown, or
  LOG ONLY rules.
- Cooldown and fresh-event handling reuse the existing alert bookkeeping rather
  than adding another timestamp to every live `Detection`.
- LOG's DEVICES and EVENTS views share the existing BlackBox page buffer. There
  is no second timeline database or duplicate resident history cache.
- Device policy records are compact fixed 8-byte entries (MAC + type + policy)
  instead of reserving alias storage for every row.
- The v1.21 LOG sparkline is opportunistic: names and timestamps always win on
  narrow 240-pixel layouts, so the chart disappears rather than overlapping
  identity text.
- Historical BlackBox records remain honest about their limits: evidence and
  RSSI history were not stored by older rows and are not reconstructed or
  invented after reboot.

**Migration and compatibility**
- Existing v1.20.1 per-device IGNORE records migrate into the new policy format.
  Both the typed `dev` format and older MAC-only `macs` format are supported.
- Migration is transactional: legacy keys are removed only after the complete
  new-format write succeeds, and failed writes leave the source data intact.
- BlackBox format, SD CSV format, and the existing detection-history storage
  remain unchanged.
- The normal 3.2-inch CYD/ST7798 profile, its optional 80 MHz display variant,
  Freenove 3.2-inch, AWOK 2.4-inch, RL Phantom 2.4-inch, 2.8-inch CYD variants,
  and LilyGo T-Watch S3 beta remain in the release matrix.
- T-Watch keeps its stock Arduino Wi-Fi driver path, existing global haptic
  control, BLE LISTEN / SLEEP CPU settings, radio self-heal, and lock-screen
  security behavior.

**Validation**
- Stages A-E were developed as separate reviewed changes with the full firmware
  board matrix, host tests, and native/WASM emulator regression gates.
- The final lab candidate was built through the same release pipeline used for
  production, including merged-image assembly, manifest stamping, OTA signing,
  exact Pages-site validation, and preservation of the live v1.20.1 production
  flasher.
- OTA firmware is signed with the same key whose public point is compiled into
  the firmware; the release pipeline verifies the key match before publishing.
